Article Title: 'I have not come here for regime change': Dhruv Rathee during CJP protest in Bengaluru

NEW DELHI: YouTuber Dhruv Rathee on Thursday said, “I have not come here for regime change”, while participating in a protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, demanding his immediate resignation over alleged irregularities in the SIR, news agency PTI reported.Rathee joined CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and actor-activist Prakash Raj at Freedom Park, where they took part in a protest organised under the banner of ‘Janata Nyayalaya’ against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The protesters demanded the immediate resignation of Kumar over alleged irregularities in the SIR exercise.Addressing the gathering in Bengaluru, Rathee said, “I have not come here for regime change.” He also alleged that there was “zero transparency and zero accountability from the EC” over the SIR exercise.Dipke said protesters would continue their agitation until Kumar stepped down. “We will hit streets, reclaim democracy, continue agitation till CEC resigns,” Dipke said.Actor Prakash Raj further demanded that the SIR exercise be scrapped, alleging that it was not merely about deletion of votes but also concerned the dignity and rights of citizens.He also alleged that CEC Gyanesh Kumar was “acting at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah”.A large number of women, students and other members of civil society gathered at Freedom Park, with protesters raising slogans demanding that the SIR exercise be scrapped and Kumar resign.According to organisers, the protest was organised as a “people's tribunal” for people affected by the SIR exercise across Karnataka. They said it would be followed by a “Chappal protest” in solidarity with women.Posters at the protest carried slogans including “Error 404 - Name Not Found”, “It's done bro, resign sir” and “Don't erase us, hear us”.Police said tight security arrangements had been put in place at the venue to prevent any untoward incident.
Article Summary: YouTuber Dhruv Rathee took part in a protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar. Protesters demanded his immediate resignation over alleged irregularities in the SIR exercise. Rathee alleged that there was “zero transparency and zero accountability from the EC’

Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Thursday condemned recent attacks on two airports in Saudi Arabia's Riyadh by Yemen's Iran-linked Houthi group, calling the targeting of civilian infrastructure “completely unacceptable”.MEA issued a statement saying that the attacks on Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh had resulted in civilian deaths and injuries.“India condemns the attacks over the past few days targeting Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, which have resulted in civilian deaths and injuries,” the MEA said.READ ALSO: Malaysia bets on AI boom with 2,300-acre Silicon Island “The targeting of civilian infrastructure is completely unacceptable. We express our deepest condolences to the families of those who have lost their loved ones. We wish speedy recovery for those injured. We express solidarity and stand with the people and government of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia,” it added.Three people were killed and 36 injured in attacks on the two Saudi airports over two days, according to Saudi authorities cited by the BBC.Two people were killed and 28 wounded in an attack on Abha International Airport, the General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) said on Wednesday.In a separate attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, one person was killed and eight others were injured, it said. The attacks took place on October 6 and 7, although GACA did not specify which airport was targeted on each day.Two women, who were Moroccan and Algerian nationals, were among those killed in the Abha attack, according to GACA.The attacks, for which the Houthis have claimed responsibility, mark an escalation in the renewed fighting between Saudi-backed government forces and the Iran-aligned Houthi group in Yemen.Saudi Arabia’s civil aviation authority did not identify those responsible for the attacks. However, Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the group had targeted both Saudi airports with ballistic missiles and drones.Saree also claimed that the Houthis attacked Aden International Airport in Yemen on Wednesday. The airport is a major international gateway for areas of Yemen outside Houthi control and has been targeted during previous bouts of fighting.He said the attacks on the Saudi airports were carried out in “response to the Saudi aggression against our country”, which he claimed involved “60 airstrikes and missile attacks in the past 24 hours”.Earlier in the day, the Houthi group also issued a “last warning” to global airlines operating flights through Saudi airspace, saying the area had become a “theater for our military operations”.The group also claimed it had attacked King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh with a ballistic missile. There was no immediate confirmation from Saudi Arabia of the latest claim.Saree said the missile “struck its target with precision and caused the disruption of airport operations.”“We reiterate our call and warning "for the last time" to all global airlines regarding the consequences of continuing to operate flights in Saudi airspace, which has become a theater for our military operations,” Saree said.He added that airspace over the “sacred areas” in Mecca and Medina was exempt from the warning. The Houthi warning came amid heightened concerns over attacks on Saudi airports and airspace.The US Mission in Saudi Arabia on Wednesday urged American citizens to exercise heightened vigilance amid Houthi threats. It warned that the situation could lead to flight cancellations, airspace closures and other travel disruptions.
Article Summary: India condemns recent attacks on two airports in Saudi Arabia's Riyadh by Yemen's Iran-linked Houthi group. Three people were killed and 36 injured in attacks on the two Saudi airports over two days, according to Saudi authorities. Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the group had targeted both Saudi airports with ballistic missiles and drones.

NEW DELHI: Weeks after the alleged suicide of a postgraduate medical student in Surat triggered fresh concerns over harassment and ragging in medical colleges, the National Medical Commission (NMC) has sought a para-wise report within 24 hours from MGM Medical College and MY Hospital, Indore, on allegations of mental harassment, public humiliation and academic intimidation of a first-year postgraduate resident.The complaint concerns Dr Simmi Yadav, a first-year postgraduate resident in the Department of Obstetrics & Gynaecology. Filed by her brother, it alleges that she attempted suicide by insulin overdose and is currently in the intensive care unit.The case comes amid continuing concerns over the treatment of junior doctors and medical students. In a December 2024 advisory, the NMC said it continued to receive numerous complaints involving undergraduate and postgraduate students, including cases of mental harassment and instances leading to suicide.The complaint alleges that Dr Simmi was repeatedly humiliated over minor mistakes, threatened with adverse academic consequences and made to undertake non-academic work. The NMC has directed the college to examine the allegations against the concerned residents and faculty and furnish their responses.The commission has sought her duty rosters, attendance and biometric records, handover registers and leave records to verify allegations that she was working 14-15 hours despite an official roster showing around 12-hour duties.It has also ordered confidential interactions with other PG residents to ascertain whether similar instances of harassment, intimidation or coercion have been reported. The college has been asked to preserve WhatsApp messages, emails, complaints, duty and academic records and other evidence.The NMC has further sought details of the functioning of the college's Anti-Ragging Committee and Squad, counselling and mental-health support available to PG residents, and compliance with anti-ragging regulations.The regulator's own National Task Force on the mental health of medical students found that 26.7% of respondents reported harassment by senior postgraduate students in clinical settings, highlighting concerns about the working environment faced by junior doctors.The commission has directed the college to ensure that Dr Simmi does not face retaliation, victimisation or adverse academic treatment for raising the complaint or participating in the inquiry. The Action Taken Report, supported by documents, has to be submitted within 24 hours.
Article Summary: The National Medical Commission has sought a para-wise report within 24 hours from MGM Medical College and MY Hospital, Indore. The complaint concerns Dr Simmi Yadav, a first-year postgraduate resident in the Department of Obstetrics & Gynaecology. Article Title: Congress protest: Delhi Police to scan videos to identify protesters accused of assaulting personnel; FIR likely

NEW DELHI: The Delhi Police is examining several mobile phone videos to identify protesters allegedly involved in the assault and obstruction of police personnel during a Congress protest near Jantar Mantar, police sources said on Thursday.The footage, including videos showing women police officers and constables allegedly being assaulted, is being analysed to establish the sequence of events and identify those involved, the sources said, as cited by news agency PTI.The police are also examining footage from other sources to identify people who allegedly manhandled or obstructed personnel deployed to maintain law and order during the protest.Delhi Police is likely to register an FIR under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) relating to assault on public servants, obstructing public servants in the discharge of their duties and other applicable sections, the sources said.The investigation comes after Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi , along with their supporters, staged protests on Tuesday and Wednesday over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Around 90 people, including Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi, were detained by Delhi Police on Wednesday after they were stopped from proceeding towards Jantar Mantar.Both leaders were later released from police detention a little after 8 pm.Rahul Gandhi was taken to Barakhamba police station, while Priyanka Gandhi was taken to Chhatrasal Stadium, officials said.The latest video examination is also taking place amid police action over social media posts related to the protests.The Delhi Police had asked a social media platform to remove or restrict access to 11 posts and videos that it alleged presented a misleading account of police action during a recent protest.In notices issued under the Information Technology Act, the police alleged that some protesters had pushed against personnel, removed or jumped over barricades and attempted to proceed despite restrictions imposed under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS).The police said personnel subsequently restrained or detained some protesters while discharging their duties.According to the notice, some videos “appear to be selectively” portraying the subsequent police intervention as “misbehaviour or unwarranted use of force”, while allegedly leaving out the preceding acts of obstruction, resistance and non-compliance.The police described the portrayal as “selective, misleading and contextually incomplete” and said it could create a false narrative about the conduct of its personnel, provoke public reaction and undermine confidence in law-and-order measures.Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi were among opposition leaders and Congress workers who travelled towards Jantar Mantar on Wednesday, but police stopped them from proceeding further.The protesters then staged a sit-in near a roundabout close to the Shangri-La hotel in central Delhi.Priyanka Gandhi and several women leaders lay on the road while carrying a copy of the Constitution. Security personnel subsequently removed the protesters from the spot.“This is how they treat members of Parliament who are asking simply to meet the election commissioners. This is how they treat us. They are beating members of Parliament,” Priyanka Gandhi said.The detentions came a day after Delhi Police registered an FIR against Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi and their supporters over allegations that they forcibly entered Akashvani Bhawan during a protest on October 6.Police said the FIR followed a complaint alleging that the two Congress leaders, their supporters and other MPs entered the premises without permission.Medico-legal examinations were also conducted on two security guards who allegedly sustained injuries when protesters tried to enter the building.On Tuesday, Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi were among around 260 people detained after an over eight-hour sit-in inside Akashvani Bhawan following an opposition march towards the Election Commission office.Delhi Police had said no application seeking permission for the march had been submitted to the Deputy Commissioner of Police, New Delhi, and no permission had been granted.
Article Summary: Delhi Police is examining several mobile phone videos to identify protesters allegedly involved in the assault and obstruction of police personnel during a Congress protest. The investigation comes after Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi, along with their supporters, staged protests on Tuesday and Wednesday. Delhi Police is likely to register an FIR under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

Article Title: India’s first high-altitude snow leopard safari flagged off in Ladakh
Article Text:
File photo: Ladakh Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena

LEH/JAMMU: Ladakh lieutenant governor, Vinai Kumar Saxena, Wednesday flagged off India’s first high-altitude wildlife safari focused on snow leopard trails, with an aim of making local communities “equal partners in protecting and promoting Ladakh’s wildlife and benefiting economically”.“Wildlife should not be protected at the cost of people, nor should development come at the cost of wildlife. We must create a model in which both can thrive together,” the LG said after flagging off six safari vehicles.The project, operated by the Snow Leopard and High-Altitude Nature Conservation (SHAN) Society in collaboration with the UT’s forest department, has mapped the safari routes through Hemis National Park, Changthang and Karakoram Wildlife Sanctuary, besides Nubra, Zanskar, Sham, Kargil, and Drass districts.Ladakh has 477 snow leopards out of 477 across India. The region is also home to more than 38 mammal species, over 340 bird species, and around 1,800 vascular plant species.
Article Summary: Ladakh lieutenant governor, Vinai Kumar Saxena, Wednesday flagged off India’s first high-altitude wildlife safari focused on snow leopard trails. The project, operated by the Snow Leopard and High-Altitude Nature Conservation (SHAN) Society, has mapped safari routes through Hemis National Park, Changthang and Karakoram Wildlife Sanctuary.

NEW DELHI: Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma's claim that Mumtaz Begum, a 43-year-old woman who was sent to Bangladesh in June, is safe and in daily touch with her son has left her family with questions.Her son, Momruz Ali (26), told TOI Wednesday that he has had no contact with his mother and received no official communication from authorities about her whereabouts. Ali saidOn Sept 3, Gauhati HC directed the external affairs ministry to locate Mumtaz in Bangladesh and bring her back to pursue her case before the foreigners tribunal.It ordered Rs 2 lakh interim compensation for her husband, noting she had been expelled without an adult family member being informed.Declared a foreigner in 2019, Mumtaz had got relief from the HC in April this year, which set aside the tribunal's opinion and ordered fresh consideration of her case, citing deficiencies in its assessment of voter-list records and other citizenship documents. Doubling down on India’s stand that sea lanes must not be turned into war zones and proposal to end conflict on Black Sea, PM Narendra Modi said oceans don’t separate countries but these connect them while calling for a free, open, secure and rules-based maritime order.In a message that was read out at Great Oceans Dialogue in Delhi, PM said, “The oceans do not separate us, they connect us, because what happens in one part of the world can have an impact far beyond its shores...Our vision is a free, open, secure and rule-based maritime that brings greater peace, prosperity and progress for all.” Modi said India’s maritime vision extends across regions and oceans, and is built on “cooperation, trust, mutual respect and mutual benefit”.His remarks come amid efforts to push a maritime understanding between Russia and Ukraine to keep the Black Sea open for commercial shipping and prevent attacks on vessels and critical maritime infrastructure. India’s three-part ceasefire plan seeks to halt attacks on energy facilities and other critical infrastructure; continuous and unhindered movement of grain, crude oil, LNG and LPG through Black Sea ports; and a complete stop to attacks on commercial vessels, merchant ships, and maritime operations to safeguard seafarers and global supply chains.The emphasis on maritime freedom assumes significance as attacks and disruptions in the Black Sea have affected commercial shipping, ports and movement of agricultural commodities during the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war.Participating in a panel discussion, Chief of Naval Staff Admiral Krishna Swaminathan said that they don’t make any distinction between national security and national economic security. Swaminathan added that maritime security affects all nations as he stressed on the need for partnerships.The officer said that the vastness of oceans made cooperation, collaboration and resource-sharing is essential.He added all nations should maintain maritime domain awareness and share broad assessments of threats. Invoking PM’s SAGAR and MAHASAGAR formulations, Swaminathan said maritime threats are increasingly transregional because oceans are contiguous. Cooperation, therefore, must extend beyond individual regions, with regions working together for collective security and growth.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi said oceans don’t separate countries but these connect them while calling for a free, open, secure and rules-based maritime order. His remarks come amid efforts to push a maritime understanding between Russia and Ukraine to keep the Black Sea open.

Russia has welcomed India’s readiness to make a “feasible contribution” towards resolving the Ukraine conflict. On Wednesday, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said Moscow was grateful to New Delhi for its willingness to help and the ideas it has proposed.“Indeed, India is declaring readiness to make a feasible contribution to resolving the situation surrounding Ukraine,” Peskov said, according to state-run TASS, while responding to reports that India had sent a new three-part proposal for a peaceful resolution.“We are grateful to our Indian friends for such readiness and the ideas that are being offered,” he added.Peskov’s remarks come days after Ukrainian foreign minister Andrii Sybiha said India’s proposal for a possible ceasefire was the “broadest” among four offers received by Kyiv. The other proposals were from Turkiye, Egypt and the US.“We have four proposals. The broadest one is India’s proposal. We are ready for an energy and Black Sea ceasefire, but only in this combination,” Sybiha told reporters in Kyiv on Friday, according to European Pravda.India’s efforts have also received praise from Russian president Vladimir Putin.Ahead of the BRICS summit in New Delhi last month, Putin and Modi held talks during which the Russian leader briefed the Prime Minister on the Ukraine conflict and ongoing peace initiatives.On Friday, Putin said Prime Minister Narendra Modi had “good ideas” aimed at finding mutually acceptable solutions to the conflict.“Prime Minister Narendra Modi is one of those world leaders who, despite our very good and even friendly relations, personal good relations, constantly raises the question and asks the question about putting an end to the conflict in Ukraine,” Putin said.“He has an avid interest and very good ideas aimed at finding mutually acceptable solutions. In that sense, naturally, the Prime Minister takes a neutral position but with an interest in the end of the conflict,” he added.Putin also said, “I think it’s my duty to say that directly. And we are thankful to the Prime Minister for his ideas.”Modi has repeatedly maintained that India is willing to support meaningful efforts towards peace. Responding to a question on India’s role, he said, “I have already indicated India’s willingness to support meaningful efforts aimed at achieving a peaceful resolution of the conflict.”External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said on Sunday that India had moved beyond advocacy and intensified engagement with both Kyiv and Moscow. He said New Delhi was focusing on issues including the safety of shipping in the Black Sea, grain exports and energy supplies.India has consistently advocated dialogue and diplomacy to resolve the conflict, now in its fifth year. Ukraine, meanwhile, has called for an unconditional ceasefire, including an end to attacks on energy and port infrastructure and a halt to hostilities in the Black Sea.
Article Summary: Russia has welcomed India’s readiness to make a “feasible contribution” towards resolving the Ukraine conflict. On Wednesday, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said Moscow was grateful to New Delhi for its willingness to help and the ideas it has proposed.

NEW DELHI: Captain Smit Machchhar, the Indian pilot injured in a mid-air attack on a Tel Aviv-bound flydubai flight, is “recuperating well” and responding positively to treatment, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said on Tuesday.MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said Machchhar remains hospitalised in Abu Dhabi, with the Indian embassy in the UAE maintaining regular contact with him, his family and local authorities.“Captain Smit Machchhar is in the hospital in Abu Dhabi. Our embassy in the UAE has been in regular touch with him, with his family, with local authorities, and with the hospital authorities. He's recuperating well. He's responding well. The pilot suffered severe injuries to his head, neck and hand after co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami, an Omani national, attacked him during the flight and attempted to take control of the aircraft.Machchhar's condition had become critical during the incident, with heavy bleeding from his injuries and his pulse dropping dangerously low.He was kept stable during the flight by Dr Shuta Musaev, a Georgian dentist living in Israel who was the only doctor on board.Musaev told ABC News that he used T-shirts as pressure dressings and ice packs to control the bleeding for around 45 minutes. At one point, Machchhar's pulse became dangerously low and Musaev raised his feet until his pulse recovered.“When I saw his lips were blue, I told the steward, 'We need to land quickly. He doesn’t have much more time',” Musaev said.Machchhar was eventually handed over to medical teams after the aircraft landed in Saudi Arabia. He has since been receiving treatment in the UAE.The pilot has been hailed as a “hero” by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for his actions during the attack. Musaev also credited Machchhar with helping save the lives of those on board.

Article Title: Consensual relation turns sour: Woman cannot use ‘strong-arm tactic’ against man
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court has held that a criminal prosecution cannot be reduced to a “strong-arm tactic” to force a person to marry by lodging a case of rape after consensual relations did not fructify in nuptial ties. It quashed criminal proceedings against a man which were initiated by his girlfriend after the relationship turned sour after three years of courtship.A bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said consent allegedly under fear or misconception cannot be loosely inferred to fasten criminal liability on one of the parties when both admittedly had a consensual relationship and the other party willingly permitted a physical relationship. It said that a consensual relationship spread over three years has eventually ended with a criminal case lodged against the man in this case and it cannot be allowed.“Even on a bare reading of the complaint, there is no clear assurance or a promise made of marriage, since the specific allegation is that they entered into a physical relationship after courtship, fully knowing the consequences, but alleged to be under the pretext of marriage; clearly an afterthought.The respondent (the woman) is a well-educated woman, who entered into a consensual relationship and carried it on for three years, allegedly on the pretext of marriage, which never fructified. She categorically states that she would drop the charge if he marries her. A criminal prosecution cannot be reduced to a strong-arm tactic,” the bench said.Referring to the apex court’s earlier order, the bench said there must be adequate evidence to show that at the initial stage itself, the accused had no intention whatsoever of keeping his promise to marry the victim. It said there may be circumstances when a person having the best of intentions is unable to marry the victim owing to various unavoidable circumstances.“In order to come within the meaning of the term “misconception of fact”, the fact must have an immediate relevance. Section 90 IPC (Consent given under fear or misconception) cannot be called into aid in such a situation, to pardon the act of a girl in entirety, and fasten criminal liability on the other, unless the court is assured of the fact that from the very beginning, the accused had never really intended to marry her,” the bench noted.In this case, the girl met the accused at an academy, wherein both were enrolled. Admittedly, they fell in love and their family members also talked to each other. On an understanding that they would be married, he used to visit her house, where she lived with her mother and brother. When nobody was at home, they entered into a physical relationship, which continued thereafter for about three years. Admittedly, the physical relationship continued for three years unabated and later they separated.The marriage proposal mooted by both the families also fell through, upon which the complaint was raised.After examining the complaint, the bench said, “We are unable to find any criminal culpability on the appellant who entered into a consensual relationship with the respondent, whose consent cannot be said to be coerced or obtained on a misrepresentation.”
Article Summary: A bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said consent allegedly under fear or misconception cannot be loosely inferred to fasten criminal liability on one of the parties. It said that a consensual relationship spread over three years has eventually ended with a criminal case lodged against the man in this case.

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu minister Aadhav Arjuna launched a sharp attack on the DMK, claiming that the party had underestimated his side and was now in a weak position in the Maduranthakam constituency.Arjuna said the DMK had earlier claimed it would win 200 constituencies but was now sitting in the opposition benches.“The DMK, which said that it would win 200 constituencies, is sitting in the Opposition benches. They took us lightly. They said, ‘These people only know how to blow whistles.’ That very whistle came to us as our symbol, and we have blown them away completely with that whistle,” he said.Arjuna further claimed that the DMK was in a “pathetic position” in the constituency and questioned whether the party would even be able to retain its election deposit.“In this constituency, the DMK is in a pathetic position. Will the DMK even get its deposit back?” he said.He also targeted Tamil Nadu leader of opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin , alleging that his remarks were damaging the DMK.“Everything that comes out of the mouth of Udhayanidhi is only obscenity. No one else needs to come to destroy the DMK; MK Stalin’s son is enough. Udhayanidhi Stalin has come to destroy the DMK,” Arjuna said.Bypolls to the Maduranthakam Assembly constituency in Chengelpet district, adjoining Chennai, and the Dharapuram constituency in Tiruppur district of western Tamil Nadu will be held on October 6.The bypolls were necessitated after AIADMK legislators Maragatham Kumaravel and P Sathyabama resigned from their posts and joined the ruling TVK. The party has fielded both of them from the same constituencies they represented after being elected in the April Assembly election.This is the first time the TVK government is facing Assembly bypolls since it assumed office in May 2026.The Left parties, which extend outside support to the TVK government and help it retain its majority, have not joined the ruling party-led alliance. Instead, they are contesting the bypolls as a separate front.Candidates of the main opposition DMK, the AIADMK and the Tamil nationalist Naam Tamilar Katchi (NTK) are also in the fray.The Vanniyar-dominated PMK, which has considerable influence in several northern parts of the state, has not extended support to any party.A key opposition campaign plank is that the bypolls were not a natural outcome but were forced on voters after the TVK “lured AIADMK MLAs” to strengthen its numbers in the Assembly.AIADMK chief Edappadi K Palaniswami has already begun campaigning, seeking “justice” over what he has described as the betrayal.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu minister Aadhav Arjuna launched a sharp attack on the DMK. He claimed that the party had underestimated his side and was now in a weak position. Bypolls to the Maduranthakam Assembly constituency in Chengelpet district, adjoining Chennai, will be held on October 6.

Article Title: Who is Shiranthi Rajapaksa? Sri Lanka's former first lady arrested over alleged misuse of hospital funds
Article Text:
File photo: Prison officers escort Shiranthi Rajapaksa, the wife of Sri Lanka's former president Mahinda Rajapaksa, to a prison vehicle outside a magistrate's court in Colombo

What is the case against Shiranthi Rajapaksa?

Who is Shiranthi Rajapaksa?

Why are the Rajapaksas facing corruption cases now?

Sri Lanka’s former first lady Shiranthi Rajapaksa, the wife of former president Mahinda Rajapaksa , has been arrested over allegations of misusing LKR 10 million (approx 29.3 lakhs) linked to a charity she headed.The 73-year-old was arrested at her Colombo home on Wednesday by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC). She was later produced before a Colombo court, which ordered her to remain in custody until October 13 while investigations continue.The investigation centres on Siriliya Saviya, a charitable organisation headed by Shiranthi Rajapaksa. Investigators allege that LKR 10 million obtained from the state-run National Savings Bank was meant to help provide a CT scanner to Colombo’s Lady Ridgeway Hospital for Children, but that the scanner was not supplied and the funds were instead misused.The case also involves former National Savings Bank chairman Pradeep Kariyawasam, who was arrested over allegations that the money was transferred to the Siriliya Saviya account without following proper procedures. He was later released on bail.There is a dispute over what happened to the money. Shiranthi Rajapaksa’s lawyers told court that the funds remain in the Siriliya Saviya bank account and have not been misappropriated.Her defence also said the organisation had been trying to raise about LKR 160 million for the CT scanner.Sri Lankan officials have also pointed to the fact that a scanner had already been donated to the hospital by China, raising questions over the purpose of the funds collected for the equipment.Rajapaksa has denied wrongdoing.Shiranthi Rajapaksa was Sri Lanka’s first lady during her husband Mahinda Rajapaksa’s presidency from 2005 to 2015. She was closely associated with Siriliya Saviya, which undertook charitable and welfare activities during her years as first lady.Mahinda Rajapaksa dominated Sri Lankan politics for years, serving as president from 2005 to 2015 and gaining popularity after government forces defeated the LTTE in 2009, ending the 26-year civil war. His family subsequently became a powerful political dynasty, with his brothers, sons and other relatives holding key positions.His popularity waned amid allegations of corruption and abuse of power, and he lost the presidency in 2015. The family returned to power in 2019 when his brother Gotabaya became president, but his government was eventually overwhelmed by an economic crisis that triggered mass protests in 2022 and forced him to resign and flee the country.Sri Lanka’s current president Anura Kumara Dissanayake came to power in 2024 on an anti-corruption platform and pledged to pursue cases involving alleged wrongdoing under previous governments.His government has since revived several investigations involving members of the Rajapaksa family.Shiranthi’s arrest follows legal troubles involving her sons as well. Her eldest son, Namal Rajapaksa, a lawmaker and former minister, has been detained in a separate bribery case. Another son, Yoshitha Rajapaksa, was also arrested earlier this year on corruption-related allegations.
Article Summary: Shiranthi Rajapaksa was arrested at her Colombo home on Wednesday. She is accused of misusing LKR 10 million linked to a charity she headed. The 73-year- old was Sri Lanka’s first lady during her husband's presidency.

Article Title: ‘Last warning to global airlines’: Houthis attack Riyadh airport, warn over Saudi airspace

Houthis claim Riyadh airport strike, issue ‘last warning’ to global airlines over Saudi airspace

Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi group on Thursday issued what it called a “last warning” to global airlines over operating flights in Saudi airspace, saying the area had become a “theater for our military operations”. Article Title: ‘Iran will never have a nuclear weapon’: Rubio draws red line for Tehran
Article Text:
File photo: Iran will never have nuclear weapon, says US Secretary of State Rubio

US piles pressure on Tehran

US secretary of state Marco Rubio said Wednesday that Iran will never be allowed to acquire a nuclear weapon under US president Donald Trump , as Washington pushes Tehran to make a substantial reduction in its nuclear enrichment capacity as part of any deal to end the war.“Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon, simple, period and end of story,” Rubio said at a joint press briefing with Greek foreign minister Giorgos Gerapetritis in Athens.“Anything they agree to that would be acceptable to the United States has to be something that ensures that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon,” he added.Rubio’s comments came a day after US Vice President JD Vance said Washington would not accept assurances from Tehran without concrete action on its nuclear programme. In an exclusive interview with Reuters, Vance said Iran must make a “meaningful” reduction in its enrichment capacity for the US to agree to an end to the seven-month war.“If you don't want a nuclear weapon, then why do you need 60% enriched fuel?” Vance said.“If you want to show commitment to not building a nuclear weapon, don't build highly enriched fuel,” he added.Vance said Washington remained open to a negotiated settlement but would not accept promises in place of action.The comments came as the US and Iran exchanged proposals aimed at ending the conflict and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial route for global energy shipments.The secretary of state also accused Iran of building up its conventional military capabilities to protect its nuclear programme from foreign attack. He said Tehran had amassed large stocks of ballistic missiles and drones capable of retaliating against countries that attempted to strike its nuclear facilities.Rubio said the Trump administration had significantly weakened those capabilities.“He destroyed their drone programme, their drone manufacturing capability,” Rubio said, referring to Trump.“He destroyed their missile capability. He severely eroded both of those capabilities in terms of current launchers. He destroyed their navy. He destroyed their air force.”Rubio said the weakening of Iran’s conventional military had reduced its ability to shield its nuclear installations from military action.“They will never have a nuclear weapon, period, not as long as president Trump is in office,” he said.Rubio also painted a bleak picture of Iran’s economy, saying US sanctions were putting increasing pressure on Tehran.“Their economy is in total and complete freefall,” he said, blaming Iran’s leadership for spending the country’s resources on regional armed groups rather than its domestic economy.He specifically accused Tehran of funding Hezbollah, Hamas, the Houthis and militias in Iraq.Rubio said oil shipments through the strait had already recovered significantly.“There's almost as much oil flowing out now as there was before this conflict began,” he said.
Article Summary: US secretary of state Marco Rubio said Iran will never be allowed to acquire a nuclear weapon under US president Donald Trump. Washington is pushing Tehran to make a substantial reduction in its nuclear enrichment capacity as part of any deal to end the war. US Vice President JD Vance said Washington would not accept assurances from Tehran without concrete action on its nuclear programme.

Article Title: After row with wife over drinking, Noida man jumps into drain; search on

NOIDA: Noida: A 29-year-old man allegedly jumped into a drain near the Sector 81 Metro station on Wednesday night following an argument with his wife over his drinking habit, police said. A search operation was launched immediately, but the man could not be traced till late Wednesday night.The man was identified as Ravi, a native of Jainpura village in the Jalesar area of Etah district. Police also sought assistance from the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) and National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), with teams being mobilised for the search operation.Officials said the search was being conducted in the drain and adjoining areas as teams worked to locate Ravi. Article Title: Nana Patekar dies at 75: 4 days before death, actor was all smiles, dancing with Samai group, playing Shamel in Goa event; watch
Article Text:
Nana Patekar was seen enthusiastically participating in events in Goa just days before his death.





PANAJI: Four days before his death, veteran actor Nana Patekar was seen smiling, dancing with performers and trying his hand at the traditional Goan percussion instrument Shamel at an event in Goa.The visuals from his final public appearance show the 75-year-old actor in a white kurta and scarf, enthusiastically joining local artists, clapping along to performances and appreciating their art.Patekar attended the installation ceremony of Rajshri Khandeparkar as president of Samraat Club International in Dona Paula on October 4, where he also addressed the gathering.Former MP Narendra Sawaikar, who was present at the event, said Patekar spoke openly about life, urging people to serve others and make the most of their time.“I am here today. Who knows about tomorrow,” Patekar said, according to Sawaikar. He also said, “Serve as much as you can. After all, what are we going to take with us when we leave.”Sawaikar said Patekar “spoke fearlessly and frankly” at the event, taking jibes and sharing anecdotes, before joining the Samai dance group on stage.In another part of the event, Patekar was seen trying his hand at the Shamel, a traditional Goan percussion instrument, as artists performed around him.He smiled and appeared to thoroughly enjoy the moment.He interacted with artists, played the tabla and danced alongside performers. He spoke about his long association with theatre and said he wanted to continue doing plays.“Now, I don't want to do anything else. Let's keep doing this only,” he said while recalling his early days in theatre.Patekar died on Thursday after suffering a severe cardiac arrest at his residence in Goa. He was rushed to a private hospital in the early hours of the morning.Dr Shekhar Salkar, chief of the Department of Oncology at Manipal Hospital, said Patekar was brought to the hospital around 4.20am and could not be revived despite prolonged CPR. He was declared dead at 5.20am.The actor's body was sent to Goa Medical College for post-mortem.Patekar, a National Award-winning actor, was known for his work across theatre, Hindi and Marathi cinema. His death prompted tributes from political leaders, actors and admirers across the country.
Article Summary: Patekar attended the installation ceremony of Rajshri Khandeparkar as president of Samraat Club International in Dona Paula on October 4. He spoke openly about life, urging people to serve others and make the most of their time.

Article Title: Students are not anti-socials, can protest genuine concerns at designated spot, not by blocking roads: Bombay HC
Article Text:
The Bombay HC affirmed students' right to protest against suspected wrongdoing in the MPSC exams





MUMBAI: “They are students, not anti-socials’’ the Bombay high court observed orally while hearing a plea against the weeklong ongoing protests by thousands in Pune against alleged malpractices in the Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) examinations.The HC said students have a right to protest if there are genuine causes, .The HC bench of Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna said Pune is an educational hub and students “are not keen to come on roads to agitate. If they are , it would mean the grievances are serious.’’The HC said students work hard to appear for public service examinations and if they “find any hanky panky in the procedure, they have a right to protest.’’The HC also said there should be fairness in public recruitment examinations like the one held by the MPSC and students had a right to protests but they cannot block roads.While one group of students withdrew their stir, for other two the HC said they can apply for permission and change of venue which the State can then consider.The HC said students’ genuine demands be heard and sought a reply on steps taken from the State in three weeks. The reply should state department-wise vacancies. The bench saidThe State Advocate General Milind Sathe said on September 30 Maharashtra government had met and accepted 3 out of 4 main demands the students had.The first one asking for resignation of the MPSC chief Vivek Bhimanwa, the State cannot by law grant, but the State has already written to the Governor to look into the complaints made against him.A petition by Amit Supekar and another resident of Pune to seek a designated space for staging agitations and sought immediate stoppage and legal action against protestors for conducting three illegal simultaneous protests at SM Joshi Bridge, Alka Talkies Chowk and Ahilya Study Centre.The protests had begun after an MPSC examination conducted for the Drug Controller post and it was found that three days earlier, the paper had been leaked online.The students had felt that FIRs are not enough and heads must roll, hence they demanded resignation of the MPSC chief.The HC however asked students to withdraw any blocking of roads and said any prolonged stir could affect their own career paths.The CJ said Pune is known as an academic city. He said to the State, “if the students have a genuine demand, you must look into it.’’“See the plight of the parents who have sent their children to study in Pune. These children are innocent. All parents in the country are in crisis,...No message should go across the country that it is not a fit place for students, or the parents will also have their apprehension,’’ the bench said orally, expressing concern and said it would ensure the recruitment drive is taken care of and maintains fairness.The HC wants the State to inform of the steps it has taken and intends to to tackle the issue.The AG Sathe said the second demand of having 2 mega recruitment for 70000 posts also has been accepted as were two other demands of having Rs 100 as exam fees, like Rajasthan has and to make the examination offline.Pune is the State’s second largest city with a population of 70 lakh the advocate for the petitioner argued and said the protestors were blocking roads. Some protestors denied they were blocking roads.The students’ lawyer said police had given permission to hold protests on October 2 after the Ganesh festival at a particular location.The AG said after the meeting with the government, protestors had agreed to withdraw but continued and at present no permission exists for any protests and if they apply afresh for another location, such plea would be considered.“So far as affairs of MPSC are concerned, State has appointed a committee to look into it,’’ the AG said.For removal of the MPSC chief, the AG said law prescribes a process that includes an inquiry.
Article Summary: HC said students have a right to protest if there are genuine causes. Pune is an educational hub and students “are not keen to come on roads to agitate’’ The HC also said there should be fairness in public recruitment examinations like the one held by MPSC.

Article Title: Kremlin fires back after France tests nuclear-capable missile, calls strategy a ‘dead end’
Article Text:
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think France's missile test was necessary given the current tensions with Russia? Yes, it demonstrates strength No, it escalates tensions 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

The Kremlin on Wednesday criticised France's test launch of a nuclear-capable missile, saying Europe's defence identity was being built around confrontation with Russia and calling the strategy a "dead end".Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Moscow viewed the launch as a "loud and clear message", while stressing that Russia remained open to dialogue.France's defence ministry said on Tuesday it had conducted the first test launch of its latest-generation M51.3 submarine-launched ballistic missile. The test was intended to demonstrate the nuclear deterrent's capabilities amid heightened tensions between Russia and the West.The M51.3 was launched off the coast of Brittany without a nuclear warhead, France's defence ministry said. The test formed part of an operation to certify the nuclear-powered submarine Le Vigilant's ability to deploy the missile following a major maintenance overhaul.The ministry said the launch was conducted "without a payload and in strict compliance with international obligations".Although France's announcement did not mention Russia, the test came after Russian president Vladimir Putin warned the West against escalating the standoff over Ukraine by threatening Kaliningrad, the Russian exclave between Poland and Lithuania.NATO has said that none of its "exercises or activities pose a threat to the territory of the Russian Federation". Putin has also said Russia has no plans to attack any European country and wants to coexist peacefully.French president Emmanuel Macron, however, described the missile test as a clear signal."Today we are stronger. The message has been sent loud and clear for wherever it must be received," Macron said in a video posted on X showing him watching the launch.Macron said in March that France would expand its nuclear arsenal and proposed closer nuclear cooperation with European partners, including joint exercises and the possible short-term deployment of nuclear-capable assets on allied territory.France maintains about 290 submarine- and air-launched nuclear weapons and spends roughly €5.6 billion a year maintaining its stockpile, according to the figures cited by Reuters. Britain has 225 nuclear warheads, while Russia and the United States each have more than 5,000.The M51.3 is the latest version of France's M51 missile and entered service in October 2025 as part of the modernisation of the country's nuclear deterrent. Paris does not disclose its range, although public estimates for the M51 family put it at around 9,000 km or more.
Article Summary: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Moscow viewed the launch as a "loud and clear message" France's defence ministry said on Tuesday it had conducted the first test launch of its latest-generation M51.3 submarine-launched ballistic missile. The test was intended to demonstrate the nuclear deterrent's capabilities.

Article Title: Why ‘kaun se wale papa’ remark led to man’s conviction
Article Text:
The court said every rude or offensive remark addressed to a woman would not automatically constitute an offence under Section 509 IPC (AI Image)

“Dekho papa aa gaye, don’t cry.”

“Kaun se wale papa aa gaye?”





NEW DELHI: A Delhi court has convicted a man for insulting a woman’s modesty over a seemingly casual remark, “Kaun se wale papa?”, made when she told her three-year-old daughter that her father had arrived to pick them up from school. Though the two had no prior dispute, the court held that the remark implied the woman had multiple partners and questioned the child’s paternity.Judicial magistrate first class Moksha Bains, in a Sept 24 judgment, said the remark was not an innocuous inquiry about the child’s father but carried an insinuation about the woman’s sexual propriety and fidelity. “The expression, when addressed to a woman in the aforesaid setting, is not an innocuous inquiry as to the identity of a person,” the judge observed, adding that its “obvious insinuation” was that there could be more than one man who could be described as the child’s father.The case dates back to March 23, 2021, when Priyanka Gupta was walking with her three-year-old daughter near RBI Enclave Gate in Paschim Vihar. As the child cried, Gupta told her,Girdhari Lal, who ran a clothes ironing cart at a street corner, then allegedly interjected,Gupta initially ignored the remark and, about two minutes later, handed over the child to her husband after he arrived in a car.She later informed her father-in-law, who called the police, following which an FIR was registered at Paschim Vihar East police station under Section 509 IPC.In his statement under Section 313 CrPC, Lal admitted making the remark but claimed it was not made with any “ill intention”. He also alleged false implication, with the defence arguing that Gupta wanted him removed from the street corner where he had run his ironing business for seven years.Rejecting the defence, the court observed: “The explanation offered by the accused that the words were spoken without ‘ill intention’ is a bare assertion. No surrounding circumstance has been brought on record from which the remark could reasonably acquire an innocent meaning.”The court said every rude or offensive remark addressed to a woman would not automatically constitute an offence under Section 509 IPC, as the insult must have the requisite nexus with her modesty. In this case, however, it held that the remark was personally directed at Gupta and made immediately after she referred to her child’s father, carrying a sexually derogatory insinuation concerning her relationship with men and the child’s paternity.The court held that the prosecution had proved its case beyond reasonable doubt and convicted Lal under Section 509 IPC.
Article Summary: A Delhi court has convicted a man for insulting a woman’s modesty over a seemingly casual remark. Priyanka Gupta told her three-year-old daughter that her father had arrived to pick them up from school. Girdhari Lal, who ran a clothes ironing cart at a street corner, then allegedly interjected, “Kaun se wale papa aa gaye?”

Article Title: Hyderabad woman Sandhya Reddy becomes mayor of Sydney council
Article Text:
Sandhya Reddy, originally from Hyderabad, has become the mayor of Strathfield Council in Sydney





HYDERABAD: A Hyderabad-origin woman, Sandhya Reddy, was elected mayor of Strathfield Council in Sydney, Australia, on Tuesday. According to members of the migrant community, she is the first Indian-born migrant woman to serve as a mayor in Australia.Affectionately known as Sandy, Reddy began her journey with the State Emergency Service in 2014 and was elected to the Strathfield Council as an independent councillor in 2021. In 2023, she was elected deputy mayor of the council.A lawyer by profession, Reddy was born and raised in Hyderabad, where she also pursued her education before moving to Australia in 2005. She has been living in the country ever since.Members of the Indian community in Australia hailed her achievement, describing it as both "symbolic and significant" for the country's multicultural communities.
Article Summary: Sandhya Reddy, originally from Hyderabad, has become the mayor of Strathfield Council in Sydney. She is the first Indian-born migrant woman to serve as a mayor in Australia. Reddy began her journey with the State Emergency Service in 2014.

Article Title: Jaipur man held for killing pregnant live-in partner, burying body in rented house courtyard
Article Text:
The murder came to light on Sept 27, (Representative Image)





JAIPUR: Police here Tuesday arrested a 20-year-old man for allegedly strangling his pregnant live-in partner and burying her body in the courtyard of their rented house in Prestige Garden Colony, Bindayaka.DCP (West) Prashant Kiran identified the accused as Pravesh Kumar alias Haggu. Police said he allegedly killed Kiran Rawat on Sept 23 after suspecting her of having an affair with another man. The two were related as nephew and aunt and had been living together as partners.The murder came to light on Sept 27 when the house owner found Kiran’s body buried in the courtyard. Police said Kumar had poured about two kilograms of salt over the body before digging a pit and burying her.During questioning, Kumar told police that he strangled Kiran with one hand and covered her nose and mouth with a cloth with the other. He initially tried to mislead investigators by claiming that Kiran had died by suicide and that he buried her body after panicking, police said.Kumar and Kiran had come to Jaipur from their village about two months ago. Kiran was pregnant and Kumar was living with her and taking care of her.The two used the same mobile phone. Kumar worked odd jobs to support them, police said.After the murder, Kumar allegedly switched off the phone and went to Samod on foot to visit the Hanuman temple.Police said he told them he went there to “wash away his sins”. He returned to work and stayed there from Sept 24 to 26.On Sept 27, after suspecting that the murder had been discovered, Kumar allegedly collected Rs 500 in wages from the factory owner and fled Jaipur.Police teams began searching for him after recovering Kiran’s body. Investigators examined CCTV footage, analysed technical evidence and prepared a route chart to track his movements.A police team eventually detained him on Agra-Lucknow Expressway and arrested him after questioning.Kumar is a resident of Parsa Auliya Lalpur village under Safdarganj police station in Barabanki, Uttar Pradesh.
Article Summary: Pravesh Kumar allegedly killed Kiran Rawat on Sept 23 after suspecting her of having an affair with another man. The two were related as nephew and aunt and had been living together as partners. Police said Kumar had poured about two kilograms of salt over the body before digging a pit and burying her.

Article Title: Blast at MRPL refinery sends loud boom across Mangaluru, thick smoke billows
Article Text:
A loud explosion-like sound was reported from the Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd premises on Wednesday.

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you feel the local authorities managed the situation well after the blast? Yes No 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





MANGALURU: A blast followed by a fire was reported at the CHT unit, the Hydro Sulphur Treatment Unit of Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd (MRPL), on Wednesday.The fire has since been brought under control, city police commissioner Sudheer Kumar Reddy CH said.One person, identified as Rajesh Baptist, sustained burn injuries covering around 35% of his body and was shifted to Srinivasa Hospital. He is undergoing treatment in the ICU and doctors said he is out of danger.Six other people who suffered minor injuries at an adjacent office were given outpatient treatment and underwent medical check-ups, police said.The city police commissioner, deputy commissioner and Zilla Panchayat CEO are present at the site. Police said there was no major cause for concern and that necessary precautionary measures were being taken.MRPL also confirmed that there were no casualties in the incident and appealed to people not to panic.The blast sent a loud boom across several kilometres, with thick black smoke billowing from the refinery premises. Residents of Jokatte and Surathkal reported that their houses shook and doors and windows vibrated following the explosion.The blast was also reportedly heard at Mangaluru airport, where windows of the administrative office rattled. Fire tenders and emergency teams were rushed to the refinery, while ambulances were seen leaving the premises.On the advice of the district administration, Mangaluru airport is conducting a visual inspection of vital installations in and around the airport, including the Precision Approach Lighting Category I systems and peripheral roads, to check their operational readiness.Dakshina Kannada MP Capt Brijesh Chowta said he was in constant touch with MRPL officials, the police commissioner and Fire and Emergency Services Department officials and was proceeding to the spot to assess the situation.He appealed to people to remain calm, refrain from spreading rumours or misinformation, and cooperate with the administration. Local hospitals were also instructed to remain prepared as a precautionary measure.
Article Summary: A blast followed by a fire was reported at the Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd (MRPL) on Wednesday. One person sustained burn injuries covering around 35% of his body and was shifted to Srinivasa Hospital. Residents of Jokatte and Surathkal reported that their houses shook and doors and windows vibrated.

Article Title: A billionaire's celebration for completing his biggest order from Amazon has become a huge scandal in Austria, reaching country's Parliament
Article Text:
Image credit: LuxuryLaunches

Why was a fake Jeff Bezos escorted by real police

The Amazon order behind the unusual party

Austrian toolmaker Haidlmair wanted to celebrate a major business milestone with a party that would be hard to forget. It certainly succeeded. The company marked its biggest-ever Amazon order with a helicopter arrival, live performances and a surprise appearance by a man dressed to look like Amazon founder Jeff Bezos . But the celebration soon turned into a political controversy after the fake Jeff Bezos was escorted by three real, heavily armed Austrian police officers.The unusual appearance took place in August at Haidlmair's celebration in Micheldorf, Upper Austria. The officers, however, belonged to the Schnelle Interventionsgruppe (SIG), a special police unit based in Linz. While the man playing Bezos was an impersonator, the armed security detail was genuine.The incident is now facing an internal police review, with questions over who approved the deployment, whether the officers were authorized to take part and who should pay for their presence. Austria's Green Party has also announced a parliamentary inquiry.The man playing Jeff Bezos was Cagdas Halicilar, a professional Bezos lookalike from Germany. He arrived by helicopter wearing a dark suit and aviator-style glasses, completing the billionaire's familiar appearance.According to reports, the police officers knew they were escorting an impersonator. Their presence was reportedly arranged after Haidlmair contacted Linz police chief Klaus Hübner, whom he has known for years.Haidlmair said Hübner initially found the request unusual but later saw the event as an opportunity to promote police work, recruitment and employer branding. The company also reportedly offered to cover the cost of the officers, although Haidlmair said no invoice had been received when the issue emerged. The arrangement has now raised a bigger question: why was a special police unit used to make a billionaire impersonator's entrance look real?The celebration itself marked a significant achievement for Haidlmair. The company had completed around 170 injection molds in roughly six months for Amazon. The project involved more than 650,000 components and 2,800 metric tons of steel. The molds will be used to make standardized containers for Amazon logistics centres in the US, Mexico and Canada, with initial use expected in 2027 and deliveries beginning in 2028.Amazon representative Rick Spooner also attended the event.The event included helicopter rides, freestyle motocross, live music, bull riding and food, making the fake Bezos' helicopter arrival part of an already elaborate celebration.But the involvement of the SIG has become the focus of attention.The unit is intended for particularly dangerous situations and reportedly does not have personal-protection training. Der Standard reported that the officers may have been allowed to record the assignment as overtime, potentially including hazard pay, although police have not confirmed those details.
Article Summary: Austrian toolmaker Haidlmair wanted to celebrate a major business milestone with a party that would be hard to forget. The company marked its biggest-ever Amazon order with a helicopter arrival, live performances and a surprise appearance by a man dressed to look like Amazon founder Jeff Bezos. But the celebration soon turned into a political controversy after the fake Jeff Bezos was escorted by three real, heavily armed Austrian police officers.

Article Title: From fishing nets to grey-zone tactics: Chinese militia boat enter Taiwan’s sensitive east coast - report
Article Text:
A vessel, which APEX Aviation says is Chinese fishing boat Minfudingyu 07902 is seen off Taiwan's east coast in mid-August 2026, in this handout image provided by APEX Aviation.(Reuters image)

Fishing boat joins Chinese maritime group

Why Taiwan’s east coast matters

What is China’s maritime militia?

Civilian aircraft tracks Chinese vessels

Taiwan expands surveillance amid China activity

Blockade concerns grow

A Chinese fishing boat believed to be part of Beijing’s maritime militia has been spotted operating alongside a coast guard cutter and a research vessel off Taiwan’s Pacific coast, in what appears to be the first known sighting of such a vessel in the strategically sensitive waters.The vessel, identified as the Minfudingyu 07902, was detected more than 30 nautical miles off Taiwan’s eastern Hualien county in August, according to a surveillance report by Taiwan-based Apex Aviation reviewed by Reuters. The report used radar screenshots, infrared imagery and automatic identification system data to track the vessels.The sighting comes as China has stepped up activity along Taiwan’s east coast since June, with regular coast guard patrols in an area Taipei considers crucial for potential wartime supply routes from its allies. Taiwanese officials have said the growing presence of Chinese military, paramilitary and civilian vessels could be part of preparations for a possible maritime blockade.The Minfudingyu 07902 was identified as a fishing vessel that doubles as a Chinese maritime militia boat. According to the Apex report, it was operating alongside Chinese coast guard cutter 2502 and the research vessel Xiang Yang Hong 03 on a day in mid-August.Two senior Taiwanese officials briefed on the incident confirmed that the three vessels had been operating near Taiwan at the time. They said Taiwanese authorities had identified the fishing boat as belonging to the People's Liberation Army's maritime militia fleet.One of the officials said the vessel was operating "in coordination with Chinese coast guard maritime harassment drills"."The purpose of militia boats is to conduct substantive harassment," the official said.The second official said the three vessels were operating "in an area not commonly used by Chinese vessels" and had been "designated for heightened monitoring".The officials spoke on condition of anonymity because of the sensitivity of the issue.Taiwan's defence ministry told Reuters that China was increasingly using civilian and official vessels together in activities it described as harassment operations.China was "using law enforcement and scientific research as cover for harassment, seeking to expand their scope of operations during a non-conflict scenario to create an illusion of de facto jurisdiction," Taiwan's defence ministry said in a statement.The ministry said such activities undermine international order and challenge Taiwan's maritime rights. It added that Taiwan's military was using reconnaissance capabilities to monitor Chinese activity in coordination with other agencies, including the coast guard.China's Taiwan Affairs Office and defence ministry did not respond to Reuters requests for comment.The latest sighting is notable because Chinese maritime militia vessels have traditionally been more commonly associated with disputed areas in the South China Sea.Taiwan lies across the Taiwan Strait from mainland China, but its eastern coastline opens into the wider Pacific. Taipei considers these waters strategically important because they could provide access to supply routes from countries supporting Taiwan in the event of a conflict or blockade.Taiwanese officials have increasingly warned that Beijing could seek to rehearse a blockade by combining military, coast guard, maritime militia and civilian vessels.The activity along Taiwan's east coast has intensified since June, when Chinese coast guard vessels began making regular patrols in the area.The presence of a maritime militia boat alongside a coast guard cutter and a research vessel therefore provides another example of the overlapping use of China's maritime assets, according to Taiwanese officials and analysts.China considers Taiwan part of its territory and has not ruled out the use of force to bring the island under its control. Taiwan rejects Beijing's sovereignty claims and maintains its own government and military.China's maritime militia is made up largely of fishing vessels whose crews receive training and support to operate in disputed waters.The practice dates back to the 1950s, and the vessels have become a familiar feature around maritime flashpoints in the South China Sea.Analysts say the militia allows Beijing to reinforce its maritime claims while retaining a civilian appearance. Fishing vessels can operate alongside coast guard and other government ships, making it harder to clearly distinguish between civilian activity and state-directed operations.The vessels have previously been observed in disputed waters in the South China Sea, where China has sought to assert its territorial and maritime claims.The August sighting off Taiwan's eastern coast is notable because of the location and the combination of vessels involved.The Taiwanese officials said the Minfudingyu 07902 was already being tracked as part of the PLA's maritime militia fleet.The new details emerged from a surveillance operation conducted by Apex Aviation, a Taiwanese company better known for pilot training and charter flights.According to its report, one of the company's reconnaissance aircraft detected a group of Chinese vessels more than 30 nautical miles off Hualien.Apex declined to disclose the precise date of the sighting, citing safety concerns linked to counter-reconnaissance measures against its operations.The company documented the vessels using radar screenshots, infrared imagery and automatic identification system data.The three vessels were spread across an area covering roughly 10 nautical miles, according to Honor Hung, Apex's defence and security director."Chinese warships, coast guard vessels, research ships and some civilian vessels continue to operate in overlapping ways, "creating pressure in the waters surrounding Taiwan"," Hung said.However, he cautioned that a single surveillance operation could not establish what the individual vessels were doing or determine whether the three ships were coordinating their activities.Apex's surveillance aircraft is equipped with a powerful US-made radar capable of detecting objects on the sea surface as small as 900 square centimetres, or about 140 square inches.The private patrol also reflects Taiwan's broader effort to involve civilian organisations and companies in capabilities linked to its "whole of society resilience" initiative.The initiative seeks to strengthen Taiwan's ability to respond to potential military and other security contingencies by drawing on resources beyond the armed forces.Apex said its patrols are independently conducted and are not carried out on behalf of the Taiwanese government.Still, the company's surveillance activities provide an additional source of information on Chinese movements around Taiwan at a time when Taipei is closely monitoring the waters surrounding the island.Taiwan's defence ministry said its military was using reconnaissance tools alongside other government agencies to track Chinese activity.Taiwanese officials have increasingly focused on the possibility that China could use a combination of military and non-military vessels to restrict access to the island without immediately launching a full-scale invasion.A maritime blockade could potentially target Taiwan's commercial shipping and disrupt the movement of essential supplies while using coast guard and civilian vessels to create pressure around the island.Taiwan's east coast would be particularly important in such a scenario because it faces the Pacific and could serve as an alternative route for supplies and support from Taiwan's partners.The appearance of a Chinese maritime militia vessel in those waters therefore adds to concerns in Taipei about the expanding geographical scope of China's maritime operations.The August patrol does not by itself establish that Beijing was rehearsing a blockade, and Apex said its surveillance could not determine the specific missions of the three vessels.But Taiwanese authorities have placed the vessels under heightened monitoring as China continues to increase maritime activity around the island.
Article Summary: Vessel identified as the Minfudingyu 07902 was detected more than 30 nautical miles off Taiwan’s eastern Hualien county in August. It was operating alongside Chinese coast guard cutter 2502 and research vessel Xiang Yang Hong 03. Taiwanese officials have said the growing presence of Chinese military, paramilitary and civilian vessels could be part of preparations for a possible blockade.

Article Title: ‘Haath hamara nahi uthega’: CJP's Ashutosh Ranka alleges right-wing fringe groups mobilised to unleash violence on peaceful protesters
Article Text:
A protest organized by the Cockroach Janta Party is scheduled for October 10 at Jantar Mantar

Poll Vote & Share your view Should universities discourage students from participating in protests? Yes, for their safety. No, students should have the freedom to protest. Only in certain circumstances. I am indifferent. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





NEW DELHI: Ahead of the proposed October 10 protest at Jantar Mantar, Ashutosh Ranka has alleged that right-wing fringe groups have been mobilised from across the country to unleash violence against peaceful protesters, while asserting that the demonstration will remain peaceful.“Haath hamara nahi uthega,” Ranka said in a post on social media, adding that any violence against people would not be tolerated. He also addressed Union home minister Amit Shah, saying, “India is watching. This time, it will not be about Delhi Police .”The proposed protest is being organised by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which has not been granted permission by Delhi Police so far.Meanwhile, Delhi Police have stepped up preparations to prevent a repeat of the large mobilisation during the outfit’s previous protest in the capital. Police have asked station house officers across the city to monitor around 2,800 people identified through the facial recognition system as having alleged criminal antecedents and ascertain whether any of them are moving towards New Delhi district.Police are also tracking those who helped arrange logistics for the previous agitation, including bus operators and other resource providers, and checking whether they have again been contacted for the October 10 protest.Local police have been asked to monitor bus bookings and organised movement of groups towards Delhi and New Delhi district. Entry routes from Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan and other adjoining areas are also under heightened surveillance, with barricades planned at key entry points.Officers have additionally been directed to engage with universities, colleges and PG accommodation owners and advise them to discourage students from joining the proposed demonstration.The October 10 protest comes months after the CJP-led agitation over the alleged NEET-UG paper leak in July, when thousands of protesters attempted to march towards Parliament and sought the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.Police said 2,873 people who attended or were present near the July agitation at Jantar Mantar were identified as having alleged criminal antecedents. Of these, nearly 989 were allegedly linked to heinous offences. Police claimed 101 had been booked in murder cases, including 42 allegedly involved in two or more murder cases and 12 who had been booked in 10 or more murder cases.CJP spokesperson Saurav Das informed police on Wednesday about the planned October 10 protest.Since October 1, Delhi Police have requisitioned at least 20 companies of Central Armed Police Forces, deployed in and around Jantar Mantar. Nearly 4,000 security personnel have been deployed across the New Delhi area, while temporary detention facilities at stadiums are also being considered in case large numbers of protesters arrive and refuse to disperse.
Article Summary: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has not been granted permission by Delhi Police so far. Police have stepped up preparations to prevent a repeat of the large mobilisation during the outfit’s previous protest in the capital. Delhi Police have requisitioned at least 20 companies of Central Armed Police Forces, deployed in and around Jantar Mantar.

Article Title: 'Developed cracks after quake': 21-year-old pregnant woman, 2 kids dead as building collapses in Delhi's Seemapuri
Article Text:
Those killed in Wednesday’s collapse included a 12-year-old unidentified girl; Gulafsha, a 21-year-old woman who was around four months pregnant.

Building developed cracks after quake a day earlier: Residents





NEW DELHI: Three people, including two children, died as a five-storey building collapsed in Seemapuri in northeast Delhi.This comes a month after a paying guest facility housing Delhi University students collapsed in south Delhi’s Satya Niketan, killing seven people.Those killed in Wednesday’s collapse included a 12-year-old unidentified girl; Gulafsha, a 21-year-old woman who was around four months pregnant; and a young child whose age has not been ascertained yet. An officer said the girl’s body was recovered from the debris, with her head severed. Eight others were pulled out from the rubble with injuries.The injured persons have been identified as Momin Mirja (56), Abdaan (3), Abdul Rehman (28), Devruddin (28), Salma (50), Chote (34), Sakina (35) and Samad (30). While some of them were inside the building when the structure collapsed, others were sitting on the roadside.The building, located in E-Block near Idgah Machhli Mandi, collapsed around 3.10-3.15pm in a densely populated slum area. Delhi Fire Service received the call around 3.30pm and rushed fire tenders and rescue teams to the spot. Delhi Police, MCD and Delhi Disaster Management Authority teams also joined the operation, while an NDRF team reached the site later.In a post on X Wednesday night, CM’s office said rescue and relief operations were underway at the site. “Every effort is being made to safely rescue those trapped under the debris and provide prompt medical care to the injured. Chief minister Rekha Gupta has directed all agencies concerned and officers to maintain close coordination, expedite rescue efforts and ensure all necessary assistance and care for those affected. The situation is being continuously monitored,” it stated.MCD said the structure stood on a plot belonging to Delhi Urban Shelter Improvement Board (DUSIB), measuring about 25 square yards, and was 20-25 years old. Officials described it as a ground-plus-three-storey building, while local residents said it had five storeys.The collapse damaged two adjoining buildings, with portions of the walls of one structure also coming down. The boundary wall of a nearby idgah was damaged as well.Local residents told MCD officials that several ragpicker families lived in the vicinity and were collecting plastic and other recyclable material when the building collapsed. They also said the building had developed cracks following the earthquake reported in the area a day earlier. They claimed the owner had subsequently been trying to vacate the structure. Police have not verified these claims.Rescue teams used heavy machinery to clear the rubble and search for survivors. Four JCB machines and several ambulances were deployed at the site. Sniffer dogs were also called in to aid the rescue operation. Power supply to the area was cut after the collapse damaged an electricity pole and snapped wires leading towards the nearby market.Rescuers faced difficulties because of the narrow lanes and densely populated surroundings. Generators were used to illuminate the site as teams continued the search into the evening.Officials said the exact cause of the collapse would be established after a detailed structural assessment.
Article Summary: The building, located in E-Block near Idgah Machhli Mandi, collapsed around 3.10-3.15pm in a densely populated slum area. Those killed in Wednesday’s collapse included a 12-year-old unidentified girl; Gulafsha, a woman who was around four months pregnant; and a young child whose age has not been ascertained.

Article Title: A cloud of dust, cries under rubble: How residential building collapse in Delhi triggered panic
Article Text:
Residents pulled out four people, including a child, before authorities arrived.
