NEW DELHI: Gulafsa, four months pregnant, started calling her father from under the debris of the collapsed building in New Seemapuri at 4pm. “I can’t breathe. Please give me water. I don’t want to die here, Abbu,” the 21-year-old kept repeating until 6.30pm, when the last call came. She was found dead around 9.30pm.The collapse of the residential building on a busy market road near northeast Delhi’s Idgah Machhli Mandi Wednesday afternoon triggered panic in the densely populated neighbourhood. Residents pulled out four people, including a child, before authorities arrived. Three people were found dead and several injured till late into the night.“I was sleeping when my house shook and a thundering sound woke me up. I ran, thinking it was an earthquake and the jhuggi was collapsing. Outside, a cloud of dust had blanketed the entire jhuggi. The tremors were stronger than Tuesday’s actual quake,” recalled 60-year-old Sakina Jahan, describing the horrifying moments.The neighbourhood is largely home to garbage collectors, ragpickers and scrap dealers. The building stood out among surrounding structures that are largely without plaster or paint.But residents said it had undergone several additions. “It was originally a two-storey structure. Around two years ago, the owner demolished the second floor to build two more. This year, two more floors were added,” said Saalam (42), who lives next door.Residents also pointed to an adjoining three-storey building that tilted earlier. Its owner informed police, following which an audit was conducted and authorities ordered its demolition, which started two-three days ago.The first and second floors of the collapsed building were occupied by the owners, their two married sons and families, while the third floor was rented out. The ground floor had the family’s scrap business, said Najma, a relative.Most family members were away during the incident. “The elder daughter-in-law had gone to her parents’ house, while the younger daughter-in-law was offering namaz at a local mosque. The father went to a godown. One son and his mother were rescued in a semi-conscious state,” said Kishore, who runs a shop nearby.The building fell towards an adjoining idgah, where children frequently play. Locals said the toll could have been higher had the time been different.
Article Summary: Gulafsa, four months pregnant, started calling her father from under the debris of the collapsed building in New Seemapuri at 4pm. Three people were found dead and several injured till late into the night. Residents pulled out four people, including a child, before authorities arrived.

Article Title: ‘South Mumbai clean doesn’t mean entire city is clean’: Bombay HC questions BMC over Mumbai’s garbage woes
Article Text:
The Bombay high court expressed dissatisfaction with the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation's waste management efforts in Mumbai

BMC lists measures taken





MUMBAI: The Bombay high court on Wednesday pulled up the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) over waste management and cleanliness in Mumbai, observing that the city could not be considered clean merely because some parts of South Mumbai were well maintained.“Everywhere there is filth… Only because Worli is clean or South Mumbai is clean, or Nariman Point is clean, that doesn’t mean entire Mumbai is clean,” a bench of Justices Girish Kulkarni and Neela Gokhale said orally.The bench was hearing a petition filed by residents of Kannamwar Nagar over the Kanjurmarg waste management facility and concerns about its impact on the health of residents in nearby areas.BMC senior advocate Anil Sakhare submitted that the situation had improved. The HC, however, said it did not find “very high progress” by BMC ward officers in addressing problematic areas concerning health and hygiene at public places, hill slopes, pavements and streets.The court directed the BMC to file a comprehensive affidavit detailing the steps taken by ward officers to ascertain the “correct position” on the ground and the measures undertaken on Gandhi Jayanti as part of the Swachhata Abhiyan.The bench also warned that ward officers could be called to court to explain the situation.The judges said they had noticed a heap of plastic near a municipal school in Jogeshwari. “Can we believe that this is Mumbai? Simple cleaning will take no more than one day. Nothing has happened. It is unbelievable,” Justice Kulkarni said.Residents of Vikhroli and environmental NGO Vanashakti have also raised concerns over rampant dumping of garbage along roadsides and in water bodies.Justice Kulkarni, referring to the role of citizens in keeping the city clean, said people followed rules and refrained from littering when they travelled abroad because there were deterrents and cameras, but “here there is absolutely no worry”.The bench said that once the system was put in place and citizens were sensitised, people would eventually stop throwing garbage on the streets. “We are looking at Mumbai to be converted into that kind of city where people themselves will go and throw everything in the dustbin,” it said.In its detailed affidavit filed before the HC on Wednesday by Sakhare to show compliance, the BMC said it had held a meeting in August pursuant to earlier court directions to discuss issues relating to the Kanjurmarg facility, compliance with HC directions and measures to ensure effective monitoring.The civic body said mitigation of odour and other forms of pollution at the facility were being monitored by a committee, as reflected in the minutes of the meeting.The BMC also said it had acted on several issues flagged by the HC earlier.It said a compactor located at a heritage site had been shifted out, while the location of a chowki opposite the City Civil Court and the route and parking arrangements for garbage vehicles near the heritage building had also been addressed by shifting the garbage vehicles’ reporting point away from the court.On ward-level garbage collection, the BMC said it had placed on record a ward-level structure for collection.On illegal dumping in public areas, the civic body said it had prepared an action plan, identified garbage-vulnerable points (GVPs), installed CCTV cameras to monitor them and taken action against people found illegally dumping or littering, including by imposing fines under BMC bye-laws.The BMC also said it had undertaken public-awareness initiatives on responsible garbage disposal, including an appeal by the municipal commissioner to elected representatives to sensitise citizens on the issue.
Article Summary: The Bombay high court expressed dissatisfaction with the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation's waste management efforts in Mumbai. Justices Girish Kulkarni and Neela Gokhale said they did not find “very high progress” by BMC ward officers in addressing problematic areas.

Article Title: A video of rat in dosa, licence suspended, Rs 25 lakh demand: How Mumbai food row turned into extortion case
Article Text:
A rat was allegedly found in a masala dosa at a Borivli hotel by two sisters.

Poll Vote & Share your view In your opinion, are social media responses to such incidents helpful? Yes, they raise awareness No, they can be harmful 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





MUMBAI: A food complaint over an alleged rat found in a masala dosa at a Borivli hotel has taken an unexpected turn, with police registering an FIR against two sisters for allegedly trying to extort money from the hotelier.According to the FIR, sisters Mansi and Kinjal, along with their relatives, had gone to the hotel for a meal on September 24 when one of their relatives allegedly found a rat in the masala dosa. The family created a ruckus at the restaurant and called the police.A video purportedly showing the rat in the food surfaced on social media two days later and went viral. On September 28, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) suspended the restaurant’s licence.Police said that after the licence was suspended, the hotelier received a call from the sisters, who allegedly demanded Rs 25 lakh as compensation. During a subsequent meeting, they reportedly told the hotelier that their relative’s health had deteriorated after eating the food and that they needed money for his treatment and care.When the hotelier said he could not arrange Rs 25 lakh, the sisters allegedly negotiated the amount down to Rs 7 lakh. The hotelier eventually paid them Rs 1 lakh, but they allegedly continued calling and messaging him for the remaining amount.The hotelier subsequently approached the police, following which Borivli Police registered an FIR against the two sisters on October 5. Further investigation is underway.
Article Summary: A rat was allegedly found in a masala dosa at a Borivli hotel by two sisters. The family created a ruckus at the restaurant and called the police. A video purportedly showing the rat in the food surfaced on social media two days later and went viral.

Article Title: 2016 municipal school assault case: Mumbai court allows Mayor’s personal exemption plea but imposes Rs 1,000 cost
Article Text:
Mayor Ritu Tawde and two other individuals were granted exemption from court appearances but fined for absences





MUMBAI: Mayor and BJP corporator Ritu Tawde and two co-accused were granted exemption from personal appearance by a sessions court on Wednesday, but each was ordered to pay Rs 1,000 due to their repeated absence from proceedings in the 2016 Shastri Nagar municipal school assault case.Additional sessions judge Gopal G Bhansali directed Tawde, Zakiruddin Sayyed and Surendra Mishra to deposit the cost with the govt within a week and remain present on Nov 2 for the framing of charges, warning that in case of default, it “may issue warrants and cancel bail bonds”.The order also recorded Nov 2 as the next hearing date fixed for Tawde’s convenience at the defence’s request. Tawde’s advocate submitted that she was the “first citizen of Mumbai” and had a busy schedule because of BMC functions. The advocate also submitted that Sayyed and Mishra were social workers and were busy with their own schedules.On Sept 23, the court had granted an exemption application for Tawde and three co-accused with a cost of Rs 300, noting the accused were continuously absent and filing for exemptions despite being given a last chance.While allowing the applications on Wednesday, the judge recorded that the incident is from 2016, the chargesheet was filed in 2017 and the matter was committed to the court for trial in 2019.“Continuous absence of accused reflects their behaviour to protract the trial. Yet charge is not framed. But advocate… is praying for permanent exemption. Considering social status of accused, no non-bailable warrant is issued, and hope to co-operate the court to expedite hearing,” the judge said.The prosecution opposed the applications. Additional public prosecutor Iqbal Solkar submitted that on the last date, the court had imposed a cost of Rs 300 for exemption and that the amount was to be credited to govt. The prosecution said the matter was seven years old and alleged that the accused were intentionally avoiding appearance before the court.An advocate for three other accused said his clients attended regularly, but were suffering because of the others’ absence.The court further observed, “After framing charge, accused may pray for permanent exemption subject to hearing to be conducted in absence, without challenging identification of accused and no witness will be returned back without cross-examination.”The case arises from an alleged incident in 2016 at a municipal school in Shastri Nagar. According to the prosecution, a dispute linked to the transfer of a teacher escalated into a physical confrontation. Tawde and others are accused of using criminal force against school staff members during the incident.The alleged victims have identified Tawde as one of the aggressors. At an earlier stage, while directing the matter to proceed towards trial, the court had observed that the material on record was “more than sufficient to frame charge against the applicant” and noted that the victims had “categorically named” Tawde as the person who assaulted them.
Article Summary: Mayor and BJP corporator Ritu Tawde and two co-accused were granted exemption from personal appearance by a sessions court on Wednesday. Each was ordered to pay Rs 1,000 due to their repeated absence from proceedings in the 2016 Shastri Nagar municipal school assault case.

Article Title: 'Stabbed 7 times with dagger': How bid to seal petrol pump turned deadly for IndianOil official
Article Text:
On Tuesday morning, Mahesh Shelke (37) had gone to a petrol pump as part of a team to seal and take over the outlet.

Killed on Duty

How it all unfolded

Five arrested within 24 hours

Who was Mahesh Shelke?

IndianOil seeks ‘swift and stringent action’





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: An IndianOil sales manager died after being stabbed seven times with a dagger while on duty in Hingoli district on Tuesday. Within 24 hours, police arrested all five accused.On Tuesday morning, Mahesh Shelke (37) had gone to a petrol pump as part of a team to seal and take over the outlet. Hours later, the engineer was dead. What began as negotiations over handing over the outlet at Chondhi village in Vasmat taluka spiralled into a violent confrontation. Shelke was allegedly attacked with a dagger while others pelted stones at him, police said. Shelke was manager (retail sales) with Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL)’s Nanded office.On Tuesday, Shelke was among the IOC officials and employees who reached the petrol pump around noon to seal it and take possession following a dispute with the Pandavveer family, which operated the outlet.Talks went on for hours. The family reportedly sought a month’s time and assured officials it would allow IOC to take over the outlet thereafter. But the company team remained firm on sealing the pump. The stand-off then turned violent.Hingoli SP Shrenik Lodha said preliminary probe showed that Umesh Pandavveer allegedly attacked Shelke with a dagger during the altercation. He allegedly stabbed Shelke seven times. Some of the other accused allegedly pelted stones, creating panic at the spot.Shelke suffered grievous injuries. A Kurunda police team led by assistant police inspector Shivaji Puri reached the spot and Shelke was taken to hospital, where doctors declared him brought dead.Police registered an FIR on the complaint of IndianOil senior manager Gullakantla Maniprasad. They booked five people for murder, attempt to murder, unlawful assembly and rioting, besides invoking provisions of the Arms Act.Lodha said all five were arrested within 24 hours. Police identified them as Latabai Pandavveer (46), her son Umesh (25), and their acquaintances Shravan Wakude (21), Rahul Dhayje (37) and Prathmesh Waghmare (27).Shelke’s body was taken to Vasmat sub-district hospital for autopsy before being handed over to his family.Shelke was manager (retail sales) with Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL)’s Nanded office. A mechanical engineering graduate from an engineering college in Pune, he hailed from a village in Ahmedpur taluka of Latur district.He joined IndianOil in 2014 and served in south India before being transferred to Maharashtra in 2024. For the past two years, he had been living with his family in Nanded district.‘Heinous, unacceptable’: Puri on IOCL sales manager’s murderThe killing of an official while on duty drew sharp reactions from Union petroleum and natural gas minister Hardeep Singh Puri, who took up the matter with Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis and DGP Sadanand Date.“The issue (stabbing of Shelke) has been taken up with the senior-most officials of the Maharashtra govt and police to ensure swift and strict action against those responsible, in accordance with law,” Puri said in a post on X.Calling it a “heinous and unacceptable act of violence”, Puri said the petroleum ministry and IndianOil would extend all possible support to Shelke’s family.IndianOil chairman A S Sahney told PTI that the company had taken up the case with the “highest authorities in Maharashtra”, seeking “swift and stringent action”.“Deeply anguished by the tragic loss of our colleague, Mahesh Shelke, who was fatally attacked while discharging his official duties in Hingoli, Maharashtra,” Sahney said.
Article Summary: Mahesh Shelke (37) had gone to a petrol pump as part of a team to seal and take over the outlet. What began as negotiations over handing over outlet at Chondhi village in Vasmat taluka spiralled into a violent confrontation. Shelke was allegedly attacked with a dagger while others pelted stones.

Article Title: Firefighter dies, Hingoli cracker blaze toll rises to 3
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





The toll in Monday night’s firecracker blaze in Hingoli’s Kapda Bazaar rose to three on Wednesday after firefighter Dilip Dodke (52) succumbed to severe burns. Hours later, police registered an FIR against the deceased owner of the cracker stock for allegedly storing the combustibles illegally at his house.Dodke, a Hingoli municipal fire brigade employee, had suffered around 80% burns while battling the blaze in Marwadi Galli. The fire brigade vehicle caught fire during the operation, leaving him critically injured. He died at a private hospital in Latur on Wednesday.Police, meanwhile, booked Vijaykumar Ramkrishna Basatwar (76) who himself died in the fire, for allegedly keeping firecrackers at his house without a licence.Hingoli SP Shrenik Lodha said the FIR was registered at Hingoli city police station on Wednesday evening following a complaint by businessman Shailesh Nandedkar, who lives opposite Basatwar’s house.“Basatwar, who died in the incident, has been booked under sections 288 and 106(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and section 9B(1)(b) of the Explosives Act,” Lodha said.According to the FIR, the illegally stored crackers caught fire and triggered a major explosion. The blaze damaged houses and motorcycles and left several people dead or injured. No arrest has been made as Basatwar is the only accused named in the FIR and is deceased.The third person killed was Avinash Bangar (24) of Vanjarwada. Police said Bangar had rushed in to help Basatwar when the fire broke out. Both suffered fatal burns.Dodke, a resident of the municipal council colony, was part of the team sent to control the raging fire. The blaze broke out around 7pm on Monday and firefighters battled it for hours before bringing it under control early on Tuesday.Deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde visited Hingoli on Wednesday and, on behalf of the Shiv Sena, announced financial assistance of Rs 5 lakh each to the families of the three deceased.The FIR names at least 10 people who were injured in the blaze. Assistant sub-inspector A N Bansode is investigating the case.The tragedy has also triggered a crackdown on illegal cracker stocks across the district. Revenue and municipal teams raided four locations on Tuesday and seized 1,390kg of firecrackers from four people.Collector Rahul Gupta has directed officials to register cases wherever rules governing the sale and storage of crackers were violated. He also ordered the seized stocks to be destroyed as per norms.Several houses and vehicles were damaged in the fire, with property losses estimated at more than Rs 2 crore. The exact cause of the blaze is still under investigation.
Article Summary: Dilip Dodke, a Hingoli municipal fire brigade employee, had suffered around 80% burns while battling the blaze in Marwadi Galli. The fire brigade vehicle caught fire during the operation, leaving him critically injured. He died at a private hospital in Latur on Wednesday. Hours later, police registered an FIR against the deceased owner of the cracker stock for allegedly storing the combustibles illegally at his house.

Article Title: Popular teacher dies a day after consuming poison; four booked for suicide abetment
Article Text:
File photo

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





Police have booked four people, including a landlord, for abetment to suicide after 60-year-old Mohan Shivram Korde, a popular teacher and Phoenix English Academy director, died on Wednesday — a day after allegedly consuming a poisonous substance at his coaching class.Korde’s wife Sunita alleged he had been under severe mental stress over a long-running dispute involving the premises from where he operated his classes. She accused a builder of harassing him and pressuring him to vacate the property.Commissioner of police Pravin Pawar said, “We have registered a case of abetment to suicide against four suspects including the landlord of the premises and further investigation is underway.”Korde allegedly consumed the substance at Phoenix Classes on the Tapadia Talkies campus around 3 pm on Tuesday. After police received an alert on Dial 112, a team rushed him to govt medical hospital at Chikalthana. He died around 4.30 am on Wednesday while undergoing treatment.Police said the property dispute stretched back more than a decade. “The Korde couple had been at loggerheads with the landlord after the deal on this particular premises, from where he had been operating classes since 2001, went south.It appears that criminal as well as civil cases are being contested for the past 14 years,” DCP (Zone II) Ratnakar Navale said.Police are now examining the dispute and circumstances leading to Korde’s death.Sunita alleged that her husband had approached MIDC-Cidco police with complaints over the dispute and other issues, but was distressed over the alleged lack of action.Following Korde’s death, she approached MIDC-Cidco police and threatened that the family would not accept his body until action was taken against those named in a note allegedly left behind by him.Korde was a familiar name to generations of students in the city. He taught English through Phoenix Classes for nearly three decades and ran classes in Cidco, Aurangpura, Kranti Chowk and Usmanpura. Thousands of students attended his classes over the years.Korde is survived by his mother, wife and son, who is pursuing law studies in Bengaluru.
Article Summary: Mohan Shivram Korde, 60, a popular teacher and Phoenix English Academy director, died on Wednesday. Korde allegedly consumed the substance at Phoenix Classes on the Tapadia Talkies campus around 3 pm on Tuesday. His wife Sunita alleged he had been under severe mental stress over a long-running dispute involving the premises.

Article Title: On-duty IndianOil official stabbed 7 times, dies; 5 accused held in 24 hrs
Article Text:
IndianOil manager Mahesh Shelke was stabbed to death

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:

For box





An IndianOil sales manager was stabbed seven times with a dagger and killed while on duty in Hingoli district on Tuesday afternoon. Police have since arrested five people.On Tuesday morning, Mahesh Shelke had gone to a petrol pump as part of a team sent to seal and take over the outlet. Hours later, the 37-year-old engineer was dead.What began as negotiations over handing over the petrol pump at Chondhi village in Vasmat taluka spiralled into a violent confrontation. Shelke was allegedly attacked with a dagger while others pelted stones, Kurunda police said.Within 24 hours, police arrested all five accused, including a woman.The killing of an officer while on duty also drew sharp reactions from Union petroleum and natural gas minister Hardeep Singh Puri , who took up the matter with Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis and DGP Sadanand Date.Shelke was manager (retail sales) with IndianOil’s Nanded office. A mechanical engineering graduate from an engineering college in Pune, he hailed from a village in Ahmedpur taluka of Latur district. He joined IndianOil in 2014 and served in south India before being transferred to Maharashtra in 2024.For the past two years, he had been living with his family in Nanded district.On Tuesday, Shelke was among the IOCL officials and employees who reached the petrol pump around noon to seal it and take possession following a dispute with the Pandavveer family, which operated the outlet.Talks went on for hours. The family reportedly sought a month’s time and assured officials it would allow IOCLto take over the outlet thereafter. But the company team remained firm on sealing the pump. The stand-off then turned violent.Hingoli SP Shrenik Lodha said preliminary probe showed that Umesh Pandavveer allegedly attacked Shelke with a dagger during the altercation. He allegedly stabbed Shelke seven times. Some of the other accused allegedly pelted stones, creating panic at the spot.Shelke suffered grievous injuries. A Kurunda police team led by assistant police inspector Shivaji Puri reached the spot and Shelke was taken to hospital, where doctors declared him brought dead.Police registered an FIR on the complaint of IndianOil senior manager Gullakantla Maniprasad. They booked five people for murder, attempt to murder, unlawful assembly and rioting, besides invoking provisions of the Arms Act.Lodha said all five were arrested within 24 hours. Police identified them as Latabai Pandavveer (46), her son Umesh (25), and their acquaintances Shravan Wakude (21), Rahul Dhayje (37) and Prathmesh Waghmare (27).Shelke’s body was taken to Vasmat sub-district hospital for autopsy before being handed over to his family.The attack drew strong condemnation from Centre and the oil company.“The issue (stabbing of Shelke) has been taken up with the senior-most officials of the Maharashtra government and police to ensure swift and strict action against those responsible, in accordance with law,” Puri said in a post on X.Calling it a “heinous and unacceptable act of violence”, Puri said the petroleum ministry and IndianOil would extend all possible support to Shelke’s family.IndianOil chairman A S Sahney told PTI that the company had taken up the case with the “highest authorities in Maharashtra”, seeking “swift and stringent action”. “Deeply anguished by the tragic loss of our colleague, Mahesh Shelke, who was fatally attacked while discharging his official duties in Hingoli, Maharashtra,” Sahney said.Shelke’s killing echoes the 2005 murder of S Manjunath, a 27-year-old IOCL sales officer who was shot dead in Lakhimpur Kheri, Uttar Pradesh, after detecting irregularities at a petrol pump.March 8, 2012 | Narendra Kumar Singh, an Indian Police Service officer, patrolling Morena district of Madhya Pradesh, spotted a tractor-trailer loaded with illegally mined sandAs he tried to barricade and stop the vehicle, the driver crushed him to death under the wheelsJan 25, 2011 | Yashwant Sonawane, then additional district collector of Malegaon, spotted an illegal operation pilfering govt-subsidized kerosene from a tanker in ManmadAs he stopped to document the activity and called a supply inspector, a mob assaulted him with an iron rod, doused him in kerosene and burnt him aliveNov 19, 2005 | Shanmughan Manjunath, 27, a marketing manager for IOCL, shot dead for sealing a petrol station selling adulterated petrol in Lakhimpur, Uttar Pradesh
Article Summary: Mahesh Shelke, 37, was stabbed to death at a petrol pump in Hingoli, Maharashtra. He was part of a team sent to seal and take over the outlet. Police have since arrested five people, including a woman. The attack drew strong condemnation from Centre and the oil company.

Article Title: Mahur, Tuljapur gear up for lakhs of devotees with major safety & transport measures during Navaratra
Article Text:
Tuljabhavani temple

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





The Nanded and Dharashiv district administrations have put comprehensive measures in place at Mahur and Tuljapur shrines to ensure smooth darshan, efficient crowd control and uninterrupted essential services during the Navaratra celebrations from Oct 11 to 20.In Mahur, a fleet of 120 MSRTC buses has been deployed for devotees, while over 500 police personnel and home guards will manage queues, traffic and security. The administration has also intensified forest patrolling around the shrine to prevent wild animal-related incidents. Road repairs and restoration of streetlights along the ghat route are being expedited ahead of the festival.“More than 2,000 officials and employees from various departments will be on duty throughout the festival. Medical teams will be stationed at the foothills of the three major shrines. The temple trust has been directed to ensure drinking water, sanitation facilities, power backup and streamlined darshan arrangements,” Nanded collector Rahul Kardile said.In Tuljapur, Dharashiv district authorities have activated a 24x7 control room and placed technical staff on standby as the temple town braces for a surge in pilgrims from Maharashtra and neighbouring states.“The entire power infrastructure is being strengthened before the festival. Officials have been directed to ensure uninterrupted electricity supply to municipal establishments, as outages in high-density areas could lead to law and order issues,” a senior district official said.Meanwhile, preparations are also in full swing at Renuka Mata temple on Jalgaon Road in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar. The temple premises have been illuminated and decorated with elaborate mandaps, while CCTV surveillance and volunteer deployment have been put in place to bolster security. “Cultural programmes featuring renowned artists will be organised every evening during the festival,” Satish Vaidya, head of the temple trust, said.
Article Summary: Nanded and Dharashiv district administrations have put comprehensive measures in place at Mahur and Tuljapur shrines. More than 2,000 officials and employees from various departments will be on duty throughout the festival. In Mahur, a fleet of 120 MSRTC buses has been deployed.

Article Title: Parbhani police bust inter-state grain theft gang; 1 held, 2 on the run
Article Text:
The arrested accused with the seized goods

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





Amid rising drought-related worries and scrutiny over agricultural produce availability, Parbhani police have busted an inter-state gang from Madhya Pradesh involved in stealing stored grain from farmers.Within 24 hours of the crime, officers recovered the entire stolen property, including 10 bags of turmeric and eight bags of Tur (pigeon pea), valued at over Rs1.5 lakh. The Local Crime Branch (LCB) tracked the gang using CCTV footage and technical analysis, leading to the detention of one member.Further probing connected the accused to three grain theft cases — two in Selu taluka of Parbhani district and one in Piplod in Khandwa district of Madhya Pradesh — indicating an inter-state theft network.Parbhani superintendent of police Pankaj Kumawat credited the swift detection to focused examination of CCTV visuals and technical inputs gathered during the investigation.“Farmers are already facing uncertainty over their agricultural produce because of drought-related concerns. Theft of stored grain adds to their difficulties. Our teams immediately worked on CCTV footage and technical leads and managed to identify and detain one of the suspects within 24 hours.The entire stolen property has been recovered,” Kumawat said.The accused has been identified as Sagar Sundar Kale (20), a daily wage worker from Selu. During interrogation, Kale disclosed the involvement of his associates in the theft. Police said two other suspects, Dnyaneshwar Shankar Pawar (25) and Karan Sham Pawar (19), both daily wage workers from Selu, are absconding.LCB inspector Gajendra Sarode said the investigation had established the inter-state nature of the gang’s activities.“Technical analysis proved crucial in identifying the accused and establishing their movements. During questioning, the arrested suspect disclosed the involvement of his associates. We have recovered the stolen grain and the motorcycle allegedly used in the offence. Teams are searching for the absconding accused and investigating whether they were involved in other similar thefts,” Sarode said.Police recovered 10 bags of turmeric valued at Rs49,000 and eight bags of tur dal worth Rs50,400. A motorcycle valued at Rs50,000, allegedly used by the gang, was also seized, taking the total value of the recovered property to Rs1,49,400.The two cases registered at Selu police station are under section 334(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). The investigation also detected a theft case registered at Piplod police station in Khandwa district of Madhya Pradesh, confirming that the gang operated across state borders.Police said the arrested accused has 10 previous cases registered against him at different police stations. Investigators are now examining the gang’s movements and links in Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh to determine whether it was involved in additional thefts of agricultural produce.
Article Summary: Police recover entire stolen property, including 10 bags of turmeric and eight bags of Tur (pigeon pea), valued at over Rs1.5 lakh. Local Crime Branch tracked the gang using CCTV footage and technical analysis, leading to the detention of one member.

Article Title: Pandharpur farmers allege forceful land surveys under house arrest for Shaktipeeth Highway; statewide protests called on Oct 9
Article Text:
Farmers from 13 districts, including Kolhapur, Sangli, Solapur, Sindhudurg, Dharashiv, Latur, Nanded, Hingoli, Parbhani, Yavatmal, Wardha and Satara, participated in an online meeting on Wednesday in association with members of Shaktipeeth Highway Virodhi Sangharsh Samiti

Kolhapur





: Farmers from Pandharpur tehsil, specifically from Avhe, Bavhe, Nandore and Solankarwadi, alleged heavy police deployment, resembling a curfew-like situation, during land surveys for Shaktipeeth Highway.Jagdish Shembade, a farmer from Avhe village, said, “The police blocked all highways leading out of the village and served notices to residents the night before. When we threatened to commit suicide, the police and the tehsil administration told us to go ahead, saying it made no difference to them. They kept us under house arrest while the land survey was conducted.”They alleged that despite farmers and women threatening self-immolation by dousing themselves with petrol, climbing electricity poles and attempting to drown themselves in the river, officials proceeded with the land survey unilaterally.Farmers from 13 districts, including Kolhapur, Sangli, Solapur, Sindhudurg, Dharashiv, Latur, Nanded, Hingoli, Parbhani, Yavatmal, Wardha and Satara, participated in an online meeting on Wednesday in association with members of Shaktipeeth Highway Virodhi Sangharsh Samiti. MLA Jayant Patil, MLC Satej Patil , former MP Raju Shetti and state coordinator Girish Phonde conducted the meeting.Four key resolutions were passed during the meeting. First, farmers will submit representations and stage protests in every district on Oct 9 against alleged atrocities in Pandharpur.Second, a state-level meeting of key representatives will be held in Kolhapur on the afternoon of Oct 11 to determine future strategy. Third, farmers from across the state will travel to Solapur to protest the ongoing land surveys, which are scheduled until Oct 22. Fourth, a broad, all-party, statewide agitation will be launched.Addressing the meeting, MLA Jayant Patil said, “Farmers have demonstrated their opposition to the Shaktipeeth Highway through protests. Yet, instead of helping farmers during the drought, this callous govt is eyeing their lands. Just as the govt is attempting to conduct land surveys through deception and oppression, let us devise a counter-strategy involving the farmers.”MLC Satej Patil added, “The govt should allocate Rs one lakh crore earmarked for Shaktipeeth Expressway to drought-affected farmers and the general public instead. Even though farmers have registered their opposition through written objections, the government is acting like a dictator. We will stand firmly behind the farmers under any circumstances.”Former MP Raju Shetti stated, “Currently, there is an uprising among the people across all regions of Maharashtra, with sugar cane agitations, student protests and labour strikes underway alongside the election process. Taking advantage of this situation, the govt is sending police and goons into villages to forcibly conduct land surveys. We will give a fitting reply to this. After the sugar cane agitation concludes, we will jointly tour these districts. ”
Article Summary: Farmers from 13 districts, including Kolhapur, Sangli, Solapur, Sindhudurg, Dharashiv, Latur, Nanded, Hingoli, Parbhani, Yavatmal, Wardha and Satara, participated in an online meeting on Wednesday in association with members of Shaktipeeth Highway Virodhi Sangharsh Samiti.

Article Title: Task force recommends MCOCA on those involved in illegal sex determination and abortion rackets
Article Text:
Kolhapur

:





A state task force has recommended invoking the stringent Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) against doctors and others involved in repeated and organised illegal sex determination and abortions. The task force was set up to oversee implementation of the Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (Prohibition of Sex Selection) Act after the Kolhapur police busted a racket run by repeat offenders, including retired govt doctors. MCOCA was invoked against the accused in that case, a first in the state.Task force chief Neelam Gorhe said health minister Prakash Abitkar has responded positively and has sought the law and judiciary department’s opinion. If cleared, an amendment will be tabled in the winter session of the state assembly in Nagpur.“Emphasis will be on locating unregistered centres, curbing illegal tests conducted in homes, and controlling the online sale of portable ultrasound machines. I have suggested correspondence with central government and relevant e-commerce platforms to verify buyer eligibility and track sales records,” said Gorhe. The task force’s first meeting was held on Tuesday.After the racket uncovered by the Kolhapur police, the task force decided to direct authorities to regularly follow up the crimes to ensure suspects do not tamper with evidence and the network is effectively broken.The task force comprises MLAs Manisha Kayande, Uma Khapre and Sneha Dubey. It was decided to hold review meetings in Palghar, Pune, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Nashik and other locations before the winter session in Nagpur. Gorhe said the work of district-wise committees as well as authorised health officers in municipal corporations and Zilla Parishads will be reviewed, with action being followed up every week.Gorhe has held meetings earlier at Pune and Kolhapur. She said there is a need to draft a joint SOP for coordinated action.Kayande suggested conducting surveys, inquiries, and inspections in areas with falling female birth ratios without waiting for formal complaints. Khapre noted that assigning district-wise responsibilities to members would make operations more effective. Dubey claimed that sex determination has reached tribal regions as well.
Article Summary: The Kolhapur police busted a racket run by repeat offenders, including retired govt doctors. MCOCA was invoked against the accused in that case, a first in the state. The task force comprises MLAs Manisha Kayande, Uma Khapre and Sneha Dubey.
